chapter: Clarifications and portraits: Lester Young, Byas, Blanton, Ben Webster
title: Sorting out the 1936 chronology and Curtis Mosby's pay
summary: He corrects dates to 1936 and explains his mother's threat that kept Mosby paying him.

story.theme_name: Going west: California and the Los Angeles scene
story.community_name: Going west: moving to and working in California

blocks.x: I think there is a little discrepancy of dates back on the first tape when you mentioned leaving shortly

after high school to go to Sacramento, coming back to Los Angeles, working for Curtis Mosby and then going to San Diego. And when I asked you the date that you worked at the Mosby Club, the Memo, you said '40 something, I think or '48.
No, no, I recall the incident and I can clarify that.
No, I know what it was, you didn't give a year, you said it was after you got back from Chicago but that doesn't fit in with the chronology. You hadn't been to Chicago yet.
No, no, no.
That's what I wanted to clarify. Did you then work for Mosby again, after you had been back East?

No. No. '36 I went to Tempe with my cousin. As I said I just graduated the day before. So that had to be '36, not '37. I came back to Los Angeles and went to Sacramento in '36. I came back to Los Angeles and played the Memo. That was '36. I had my own band at the Filipino Night Club in '36.

What else did I do in '36? Oh, I giged around town with the Woodman brothers in '36 off and on when I didn't have my own group you know. And besides this job at the Mimo, Curtis Mosby formed a larger aggregation to play at the Pier in Long Beach and the clientel was mostly sailors, you know. We played and played under good conditions. The only thing is that he did-
n't pay anyone. He was a bad pay. But by my mother knowing him, he didn't hold back on my money because he knew that she would knock him down with her pocket book, her purse or draw a pistol on him.
(Laughter).
Your mother is about how big?
(Laughter.) She's about 5'2". Strong as an ox.
How big was Mosby?
Well Mosby was about the same height. He was rotund.
Desmond was tall and slim?
Yeah. And then there was a younger brother, I forget his name. He was a teenager at that time.
Desmond was a dancer?
Yes, he was with the Chocolateers, the group that put out "Peckin".
Uh-huh.
With Ben Pollack. They did this at the Cotton Club.
That's the Los Angeles Cotton Club? Frank Sebastiano Here in Culver City.
Yeah.
